# Introduction

## Which parent has more schooling

Women born just after the war were less likely than men of the same cohort to hold a degree. For every cohort since, the gap has narrowed and then turned the other way, in most European countries and in Austria too.

::: {#fig-tertiary-difference}
{{< include build/figures/tertiary_difference.qmd >}}
The female educational advantage by the respondent's own birth cohort, in 30 European countries from the European Social Survey: the share of women holding a degree minus the share of men. The measure and most of the design follow Erát [@erat2021], but the data include more countries and survey waves.
:::
